gloss: to flutter down; to fall dancing

definitions.gloss: to flutter down; to fall gently; to drift down
definitions.explanation: Describes something light falling slowly and gracefully through the air, as if dancing. Used for things like leaves, petals, snowflakes, and feathers. A poetic, evocative word.

examples.japanese: {桜|さくら}の{花|はな}びらが{舞|ま}い{落|お}ちてきた。
examples.english: Cherry blossom petals came fluttering down.

examples.japanese: {雪|ゆき}が{静|しず}かに{舞|ま}い{落|お}ちる{夜|よる}だった。
examples.english: It was a night when snow was quietly drifting down.

examples.japanese: {風|かぜ}に{吹|ふ}かれた{落|お}ち{葉|ば}が{舞|ま}い{落|お}ちて、{地面|じめん}を{赤|あか}や{黄色|きいろ}に{染|そ}めていった。
examples.english: Fallen leaves blown by the wind fluttered down, coloring the ground red and yellow.

notes:
USAGE:
An ichidan ({一段|いちだん}) compound verb combining {舞|ま}う (to dance) and {落|お}ちる (to fall). The verb evokes a graceful, floating motion. More literary and poetic than simply {落|お}ちる. Commonly used in descriptions of nature and seasonal imagery.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {花|はな}びらが{舞|ま}い{落|お}ちる (petals flutter down)
- {雪|ゆき}が{舞|ま}い{落|お}ちる (snow drifts down)
- {落|お}ち{葉|ば}が{舞|ま}い{落|お}ちる (fallen leaves flutter down)
- {羽|はね}が{舞|ま}い{落|お}ちる (a feather flutters down)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {散|ち}る: to scatter, to fall (of petals) — broader, less poetic
- {降|ふ}り{注|そそ}ぐ: to pour down — suggests heavier, more abundant falling
